### Transparent Slice Overlay & Spherical Visualizer Roll

We identified the root cause of why slices were appearing separate from workspace objects and have implemented the transparent overlay and spherical visualizer rolling across [cle_slicer.js](file:///d:/CLEJS/Dev/cle_tools/cle_slicer.js).

---

### 1. Root Cause & Alignment Fix
- **Document Structure**: JumpStart CAD stores document bodies in `app.scene.doc.bodies` (with Three.js render views in `app.scene.views`). Slicer previously queried `app.doc.bodies` which was undefined, causing it to fall back to a default sample block at `(-25, -20)` rather than extracting the user's actual 3D model.
- **Direct 1:1 World Geometry Extraction**: `getActiveBodyGeometry()` now queries `app.scene.views` and transforms vertices using `view.mesh.matrixWorld`. The extracted triangles match the exact 3D position, orientation, and spoilboard elevation of the model in the workspace.
- **Removed Artificial Opaque Stock Box**: Slicer no longer renders an artificial opaque bounding box that covers the model.

---

### 2. Transparent Workpiece Overlay
- **Translucent Ghost Body Mode**: When slicing is generated, `setWorkspaceBodiesTransparent(true)` automatically switches all workspace CAD bodies to **32% translucent ghost mode** (`opacity: 0.32`, `transparent: true`, `depthWrite: false`).
- **Clean In-Model Toolpaths**: The toolpaths (cyan rapid moves, neon green/gold/red cutting passes, orange start plane, and amber spoilboard breakthrough) now render directly inside and through the transparent 3D object.
- **Automatic Restoration**: When the visualizer is closed or cleared, `setWorkspaceBodiesTransparent(false)` restores all bodies back to full solid opacity (`1.0`).

---

### 3. "Roll Through the Sphere of the Visualizer"

We added two dedicated roll modes and spherical view controls to the HUD:

1. **`🔄 Roll Sphere (360°)` (Spherical Orbit Roll)**:
   - Centered on the workpiece bounding sphere:
     $$(\text{center}_X, \text{center}_Y, \text{center}_Z), \quad R = \text{max}(W, D, H) \times 0.85$$
   - Clicking **`🔄 Roll Sphere`** begins smooth continuous 360° camera rotation around the visualizer sphere, allowing complete spherical inspection of the slices through the translucent workpiece from every angle.
   - Click again or use the joystick/mouse to pause.
2. **`▶ Roll Slices` (Pass-by-Pass Layer Roll)**:
   - Sequentially steps through the toolpath passes from top to bottom (CNC/Laser) or bottom to top (3D additive), showing how the cut progresses layer-by-layer through the object.
   - Mouse wheel on the HUD or slider also rolls manually through the layers.
3. **Spherical Angle Presets**:
   - Quick-select dropdown on the HUD: **`[Iso 3D]`**, **`[Top (Z)]`**, **`[Front (Y)]`**, and **`[Side (X)]`**.

Large acoustic horn drivers (e.g., $550\text{mm X} \times 450\text{mm Y} \times 500\text{mm Z}$) exceed standard CNC Z-travel and cutter flute lengths. CNC-machined laminated wood/MDF creates far denser, acoustically inert, glue-receptive structures than 3D printing.

Below is our proposal to add **Multi-Part Laminated Slicing, Dowel Hole Alignment, and Tool-to-Range Mapping** to CLEJS.

```
       TOTAL 500mm WORKPIECE
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐  ▲ Z = 500mm
│ Part 13: Z 480mm .. 500mm (20mm)     │  │
├──────────────────────────────────────┤  │
│ ...                                  │  │
├──────────────────────────────────────┤  │  EACH PART GETS:
│ Part 03: Z 80mm .. 120mm  (40mm)     │  │  1. 2-4 Registration Dowel Holes (Drill)
├──────────────────────────────────────┤  │  2. Roughing Pocket passes (1/4" Endmill)
│ Part 02: Z 40mm .. 80mm   (40mm)     │  │  3. 3D Finish Contour passes (Ballnose)
├──────────────────────────────────────┤  │  4. Perimeter Cutout into Spoilboard (-0.2mm)
│ Part 01: Z 0.0mm .. 40mm  (40mm)     │  │
└──────────────────────────────────────┘  ▼ Z = 0.0mm (Spoilboard Top)
      ● (Dowel A)          ● (Dowel B)
```

#### A. Architecture & Workflow

1. **Continuous Master Slice**:
   - The entire 500mm model is sliced at high resolution (e.g., $0.5\text{mm}$ to $1.0\text{mm}$ layer height $\rightarrow$ 500 to 1000 continuous contour slices).
2. **Laminated Stock Partitioner**:
   - User specifies **Stock Slab Thickness** (e.g., $40.0\text{mm}$ or $1.5"$) and **Material Margin**.
   - CLEJS automatically partitions the master stack into discrete **Parts**:
     - `Part 01`: Slices 0 to 40 (Z: $0.0\text{mm} \rightarrow 40.0\text{mm}$)
     - `Part 02`: Slices 41 to 80 (Z: $40.0\text{mm} \rightarrow 80.0\text{mm}$)
     - ...
     - `Part N`: Top cap
3. **Precision Alignment Dowel Holes (Registration Pins)**:
   - In acoustic horn lamination, dowels are critical for sub-millimeter glue alignment.
   - **Automatic Pin Placement**: CLEJS analyzes the 2D intersection envelope across all parts and suggests 2 to 4 registration pin locations outside the acoustic flare (e.g., $\varnothing 6.0\text{mm}$ or $\varnothing 8.0\text{mm}$ dowel holes).
   - **Manual Pin Placement**: User can click in the 2D/3D visualizer to drop custom alignment dowel holes with defined diameter and depth.
   - For every 40mm part, the dowel holes are drilled first before milling the curves.

     - **Phase 2 (Roughing)**: Tool #1 ($1/4"$ Flat Endmill) $\rightarrow$ High-speed hogging/pocketing with $1\text{mm}$ stock-to-leave.
     - **Phase 3 (Finishing)**: Tool #2 ($1/8"$ or $6\text{mm}$ Ballnose) $\rightarrow$ Smooth 3D contour passes across the horn profile.
     - **Phase 4 (Cutout)**: Tool #1 $\rightarrow$ Final perimeter separation pass ($0.2\text{mm}$ into spoilboard).
5. **Per-Part FluidNC Job Export**:
   - Instead of a single unmanageable file, CLEJS exports individual ready-to-run jobs:
     - `Horn_Part01_Z0-40.nc`
     - `Horn_Part02_Z40-80.nc`
     - ...
   - Each job normalizes $Z=0$ to the top of that specific 40mm slab mounted on the spoilboard, so the machine operator just mounts slab #1, sets Z-zero, runs `Part01.nc`, loads slab #2, and repeats.

```html
### Audio Horn Real-World Examples & 30mm Laminated Stock Workflow

Your two uploaded examples represent the two classic extremes of horn manufacturing:

1. **Small 3D-Printed Bi-Radial Horn (PLA):**
   - **Characteristics:** Monolithic FDM additive printing with radial horizontal lips and circular compression driver throat adapter.
   - **Trade-offs:** Fast for small prototypes, but structural resonance, layer line ridges, Z-axis build volume limits, and poor glue adhesion make FDM unsuitable for large format acoustic horns.
2. **Commercial Altec Lansing 511B Sectoral Horn (Aluminum):**
   - **Characteristics:** Heavy sand-cast aluminum split into two halves with interior acoustic sectoral divider vanes to maintain constant directivity down to 500 Hz ($511\text{B} \rightarrow 500\text{ Hz}$ cutoff).
   - **Trade-offs:** Superb rigidity and acoustic loading, but casting large compound curvatures requires industrial foundries and tooling.

---

### The 30mm Glued & Doweled Lamination Solution in CLEJS

To replicate designs like the bi-radial horn and Altec 511B in dense, acoustically dead materials (MDF, Baltic birch, or solid hardwoods) on a 3-axis CNC router:

```
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| PART 4 (Z: 90 - 115mm): Mouth Flare Lip Slices + 4x Alignment Dowel Holes|
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| PART 3 (Z: 60 - 90mm):  Mid-Horn Expansion Slices + 4x Dowel Holes     |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| PART 2 (Z: 30 - 60mm):  Throat Transition Slices + 4x Dowel Holes      |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| PART 1 (Z:  0 - 30mm):  Driver Flange / Throat Base + 4x Dowel Holes    |
+=========================================================================+
| SPOILBOARD (Z: +0.1 to +20.1mm) - 0.2mm Breakthrough Overcut Protection |
+=========================================================================+
| ALUMINUM MACHINE TABLE BED (Z: +0.10mm Hard Safety Floor)               |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

---

### Implementation Details Added to CLEJS

1. **30mm Lamination Partitioner (`CLE.slicer.partitionLaminatedParts`)**:
   - Slices models into **30mm slabs** (with presets for 18mm, 25mm, 30mm, 40mm, 50mm).
   - Computes local slab Work Coordinate System ($Z_{\text{local}} = 0.00\text{mm}$ at stock top, $Z = -30.00\text{mm}$ at spoilboard surface).
2. **Automatic Dowel Hole Generator (`CLE.slicer.dowelPoints`)**:
   - Places 4 corner registration holes (or 2 diagonal holes) offset from stock bounds.
   - Drills completely through each 30mm slab and advances **$0.20\text{mm}$ into the spoilboard**, ensuring the wooden dowel pins seat flush with sub-millimeter registration across all layers during glue-up.
3. **Four-Stage Automated Toolpath Generator (`CLE.slicer.generatePartGCode`)**:
   - **Op 1 (Drilling - T2 1/8" Endmill):** Multi-stage peck drilling of dowel pin alignment holes.
   - **Op 2 (Roughing - T1 1/4" Endmill):** Bulk stock stepdown clearing with aggressive feed.
   - **Op 3 (3D Finishing - T3 1/8" Ballnose @ 18,000 RPM):** Fine contour passes creating smooth bi-radial curves that require only light final sanding.
   - **Op 4 (Clean Cutout - T1 1/4" Endmill):** Final perimeter cutout plunging **$0.20\text{mm}$ into the spoilboard** for clean part release without tabs.
4. **3D Visualizer Stack & FluidNC SD Export**:
   - Renders 3D gold registration cylinders (`0xfacc15`) through the visualizer stack.
   - Renders horizontal joint divider planes (`CLE_Part_Joint_k`) with elevation labels.
   - HUD includes Part Selector tabs (`[All Stack]`, `[Part 1]`, `[Part 2]`, `[Part 3]`, `[Part 4]`) and single-click **Export Part .NC** or **Part to SD** buttons to send each slab program directly to the machine controller.
```

### 1. Camera Double Permission Prompt Fixed
- **Root Cause**: When switching to Manual mode or connecting, `openManualControlCenter()` and `cle_gamepad.js` concurrently invoked `navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia(...)` before the first call completed. The browser treated them as two simultaneous requests, causing the permission dialog to appear twice.
- **Fix**:
  - Added an asynchronous promise lock (`this._isStarting` & `this._startPromise`) in [`cle_camera.js`](file:///d:/CLEJS/Dev/cle_tools/cle_camera.js#L54-L125) so concurrent calls share the same in-flight stream acquisition.
  - Removed the duplicate invocation in [`cle_gamepad.js`](file:///d:/CLEJS/Dev/cle_tools/cle_gamepad.js#L165-L170).
  - The Logitech C270 now opens with a single initialization.

---

### 2. Solid Material Slice Contour Following X, Y, Z (and A)
- **Eliminated 3D Printer Mesh Wireframe in Single Slice Mode**: Slicing solid material (wood/MDF/aluminum for bi-radial horns) no longer renders an artificial additive infill zigzag grid.
- **Exact Mathematical 3D CAD Cross-Section**:
  - Implemented [`computeObjectCrossSectionAtZ(Z)`](file:///d:/CLEJS/Dev/cle_tools/cle_slicer.js#L535-L612) which calculates the planar intersection across all triangles of the 3D CAD object at each slice elevation $Z$.
  - Generates a **3D Solid Material Slice Slab** (`CLE_Solid_Slice_k`) with true physical slab thickness in warm hardwood/timber material (`color: 0xcd853f`, opacity: 0.88).
  - Renders a glowing gold boundary loop (`CLE_Contour_Border_k`, linewidth: 3.5) directly tracing the 3D compound curve of the horn.
- **X, Y, Z & Rotary A-Axis Tracking**:
  - As you scrub the slider, the solid slice moves up and down the workpiece, expanding and contracting with the bi-radial flare profile.
  - In rotary mode ($A$-axis), angular coordinates ($A = \text{atan2}(Y, Z) \times \frac{180}{\pi}$) are tracked and displayed on the HUD DRO:
    `Slice 15/183 (Z=15.00mm | X:-25..+25, Y:-20..+20, A:0°..360°) [Solid Slice]`

### Summary of Upstream JumpStart 3D Changes (v2.7.4 → v2.7.7)

---

### 1. New Features Added Upstream

#### **New Interactive Mode: Chip Carving (`app.carve`)**
The primary addition in v2.7.7 is an interactive 3D wood carving and chisel sculpting subsystem (`app.carve`), joining existing specialized modes like `app.lathe` and `app.sketch3d`.

- **Carving Tools & Geometry Models:**
  - Support for multiple knife types: **Chip** (`tri`), **V-Cut** (`vcut`), **Stab** (`stab`), and **Sweep** (`sweep`).
  - Adjustable blade parameters: Knife angle ($45^\circ - 85^\circ$), slope side (Left / Right), blade tilt, push depth, stab length ($2 - 20\text{ mm}$), and $15^\circ$ angle snapping.
  - Interactive wood materials library (e.g. Basswood) with wood grain, sanding, and eraser tools.
- **Hardware & Pressure Integration:**
  - Stylus / pen pressure sensitivity with real-time UI pressure bar (`.carve-meter i`).
  - View navigation toggle (`.carve-hand`) allowing seamless one-finger / mouse viewport orbiting vs. cutting.
- **Programmatic API (`app.carve`):**
  - `app.carve.open()` / `close()`: Opens/closes full-screen carving studio modal.
  - `app.carve.active`: Boolean indicator for whether carving studio is running.
  - `app.carve._mesh()`: Retrieves the high-resolution deformed mesh generated by cuts.
  - `app.carve._vol()`: Real-time carved volume metrics.
  - `app.carve._chip()` and `app.carve._groove()`: Programmatic knife cut execution.

#### **Minor UI & Style Adjustments:**
- Added `.sh-more` collapsible disclosure element for secondary shape options.
- Minified variable renaming across internal utility closures resulting from the `zM` carve module inclusion.

The specifications, gear/pulley reduction ratio, and operational details for the **TwoTrees 4th Axis CNC Rotary Module Kit** (compatible with the TTC450, TTC450 Pro, TTC450 Ultra, and TTC6050 series CNC machines) are detailed below[1]:

### **Core Specifications**
* **Compatibility:** TwoTrees TTC450, TTC450 Pro, TTC450 Ultra, TTC6050[1]
* **Chuck Type:** High-precision 3-jaw chuck (zero-offset design for stable clamping)[1]
* **Clamping Diameter Range:** 
  * *Minimum:* 4 mm (micro parts)[2][3]
  * *Maximum:* 60 mm (standard cylinders)[2][3]
* **Clamping Length:** Dependent on the machine's working travel (minus the space taken up by the chuck and tailstock/thimble kit)[2][3]
* **Center Height:** 50 mm[1]
* **Total Height:** 76.5 mm[1]
* **Material Finish:** Special rust-proof coating for enhanced longevity[1]

---

### **Drive & Pulley Reduction Ratio**
* **Reduction Ratio (Sub-division / Chuck Drive Ratio):** **4 : 1**[2][1]
  * This means the stepper motor turns 4 full revolutions for every 1 single revolution of the 3-jaw chuck, balancing fine engraving resolution with mechanical stability[1].

---

### **Pulse Calculation Formula (for GRBL / Firmware Setup)**
When configuring your controller (such as Candle, LaserGRBL, or UGS) for the 4th axis, use the following formula to calculate the correct steps/mm or pulse value[4]:

$$\text{Pulse Number} = \frac{\text{Motor Steps per Revolution} \times \text{Microstepping Subdivision} \times \text{Reduction Ratio}}{\text{Cylinder Circumference (mm)}}$$

* **Motor Steps (1 turn):** 200 pulses (standard for NEMA steppers)[4]
* **Reduction Ratio:** 4 (representing 4:1)[4]
* **Subdivision:** Typically depends on your board's microstepping configuration (e.g., 16)[4]. 

**Example Calculation (for a 50mm diameter cylinder with 16x subdivision):**
$$\frac{200 \times 16 \times 4}{50 \times \pi (\approx 157.08)} \approx 81.53 \text{ pulses/mm (or steps per unit)}$$

CNC systems, particularly those with a rotary axis, maintain a fixed tool orientation perpendicular to the workpiece surface. ### 1. Review of Existing Lathe Functions in JumpStart (`xe.lathe` / `Gx`)

JumpStart includes a built-in virtual wood lathe (`window.__app.lathe` / `Gx` in [`Dev/index.htm`](file:///d:/CLEJS/Dev/index.htm#L11116054)):
- **Manual Tool Model:** Designed around hand woodturning. The user holds a virtual chisel (Roughing gouge, Spindle gouge, Skew chisel, Parting tool, etc.) using mouse/touch/pen.
- **Variable Tool Angling & Twisting:** The chisel can be freely angled, tilted, pitched, and twisted into the spinning blank in 3D space, replicating a woodworker freehanding cuts on a manual wood lathe.
- **Kinematics:** Workpiece spins continuously at 600–3600 RPM via a virtual foot pedal, while manual CSG/subtraction removes material wherever the tilted chisel intersects the revolving mesh.

---

### 2. CNC & Laser Reality: Strict Perpendicularity

A 3-axis CNC router/mill or laser cutter equipped with a 4th-axis rotary kit (such as the TwoTrees A-axis) operates under fundamentally different physics and kinematics:

```
          [ CNC Spindle / Laser Head ]
                     |
                     |  Tool is STRICTLY PERPENDICULAR (Z ↓)
                     v  No tilt / pitch / swivel (no B or C axis)
              .-------------.
             /   Workpiece   \
            |   (Rotates A)   | <--- Rotation Axis: A (around X)
             \               /       Centerline: Y = Y_center, Z = 45.10mm
              '-------------'
```

- **Zero Angling:** The spindle or laser beam is rigidly locked to the vertical $Z$-gantry pointing straight down ($-Z$). It **cannot tilt, angle, or twist**.
- **Top-Down Cutting Only:** All cutting or laser firing must occur perpendicularly onto the upward-facing surface of the material from above.
- **Two Distinct Rotary Paradigms for CNC & Laser:**

| Mode | Axis Kinematics | How It Cuts Perpendicularly | Best For |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **A-Axis Index Mode** | $A$ holds fixed angle, then cuts in $X, Y, Z$; rotates to next angle $A_k$ | Workpiece rotates to discrete faces (e.g. $0^\circ, 90^\circ, 180^\circ, 270^\circ$, or $N$-sided facets). Tool retracts ($Z_{\text{top}}$), indexes $A$, then cuts each face top-down. | Multi-sided prismatic parts, flutes, flats, engravings on multiple sides. |

| Parameter | Dimension | Impact & Machine Constraint |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |

[CLEJS] Successfully committed checkpoint: Position CNC A-axis chuck and center on object with Center Point Tool and jog-to-center functionality

### CNC A-Axis Object Positioning & Center Point Tool

We have implemented interactive positioning for the A-axis Chuck and Opposing Center, along with the precision 3D **Center Point Tool**:

```
        ============================== [ Spindle / Laser Head ]
                     │
                     │  Vertical Alignment Guide Ray
                     ▼
         .-.       ( Target Reticle )       .---.
        | C | <----+-- Workpiece --+-----> | L C | ◄── 60° Live Center Point Tool Tip
        | H |    Chuck Face      Live Center| I O |     (X = tailstockX, Y = 250, Z = 45.1)
        | U |    Center Point     Point Tip | V N |
        | C |    (X = chuckX)               | E E |
   =====[ K ]===============================|=== =|==== Z = 45.0 mm (Centerline)
   ==================================================== Z = 0.0 mm (Machine Bed)
```

---

### Key Implementations

1. **Precision 3D Center Point Tool Assembly ([`cle_rotary.js`](file:///d:/CLEJS/Dev/cle_tools/cle_rotary.js)):**
   - **Chuck Face Center Point Tool:**
     - Glowing cyan bullseye ring ($1.5\text{mm}$ inner / $5.0\text{mm}$ outer) and crosshairs in $Y$ and $Z$ right on the chuck face ($X = \text{chuckX}$, $Y = 250$, $Z = 45.10$).
     - Sharp spindle center marker cone pointing $+X$ into the workpiece end.
   - **Tailstock Live Center Point Tool:**
     - High-contrast $60^\circ$ hardened steel conical live center tip pointing $-X$ into the workpiece center ($X = \text{tailstockX}$, $Y = 250$, $Z = 45.10$).
     - Glowing target reticle with orthogonal crosshairs marking the center of rotation.
   - **Perpendicular Alignment Guide Ray:**
     - Vertical dashed gold guide ray from workpiece rotation centerline ($Z = 45.10\text{mm}$) up to safe clearance retract ($Z_{\text{top}}$), providing instant visual alignment for the CNC spindle bit or laser crosshair.
   - **Toggle Method:** [`rot.toggleCenterPointTool(visible)`](file:///d:/CLEJS/Dev/cle_tools/cle_rotary.js) to show or hide the alignment reticles.

2. **Interactive Positioning on the Object:**
   - **`rot.centerOnObject()`:** Computes the CAD object midpoint along $X$ ($X_{\text{mid}} = \frac{X_{\text{min}} + X_{\text{max}}}{2}$) and centers both the Chuck and Opposing Center symmetrically on the workpiece.
   - **`rot.fitToObject()` / `rot.clampToObject()`:** Snaps Chuck face to $X_{\text{min}}$ and Live Center cone to $X_{\text{max}}$.
   - **Step Nudges:** [`rot.nudgeChuck(±1, ±10)`](file:///d:/CLEJS/Dev/cle_tools/cle_rotary.js) and [`rot.nudgeTailstock(±1, ±10)`](file:///d:/CLEJS/Dev/cle_tools/cle_rotary.js) for incremental grip adjustments.
   - **`rot.jogToolToCenter(which)`:** Instantly positions the 3D toolhead cursor (and sends G-code jog `$J=G90 G21 X... Y250 Z... F1500` to FluidNC if connected) directly to the rotation center point:
     - `'workpiece'`: Top dead center ($X_{\text{mid}}, Y = 250, Z = \text{matTop}$) for perpendicular edge/center finding.
     - `'chuck'`: Chuck face center point ($X_{\text{chuck}}, Y = 250, Z = 45.10$).
     - `'tailstock'`: Tailstock live center point tip ($X_{\text{tailstock}}, Y = 250, Z = 45.10$).

3. **User Interface Controls:**
   - **CLE Ribbon (`Rotary & Slicer`):**
     - `Center on Obj` (`cle-r-rot-center`): Centers chuck & tailstock on object.
     - `Center Tool` (`cle-r-rot-tool`): Toggles 3D Center Point Tool & reticles.
     - `Jog Center` (`cle-r-rot-jog`): Moves toolhead directly to center point.
   - **Rotary Setup Modal (`cle_boot.js`):**
     - Step nudge buttons (`-10`, `-1`, `+1`, `+10`) for both Chuck $X$ and Opposing Center $X$.
     - `Clamp to Ends` & `Center on Object` one-click actions.
     - `Show/Hide Center Tool` and `Jog to Center Point` controls.
   - **Slicer HUD (`cle_slicer.js`):**
     - `Clamp Ends`, `Center Obj`, `Center Tool`, and `Jog Center` buttons directly on the HUD.

---

### Verification

- **Playwright Test [`scratch/test_full_rotary_axis.py`](file:///d:/CLEJS/scratch/test_full_rotary_axis.py):**

### Calibration Tests Implemented & Verified

Both diagnostic test cuts and interactive 3D visualizer previews have been implemented in [`Dev/cle_tools/cle_calibration.js`](file:///d:/CLEJS/Dev/cle_tools/cle_calibration.js) and wired directly into the **Calibration** ribbon modal in [`Dev/cle_tools/cle_boot.js`](file:///d:/CLEJS/Dev/cle_tools/cle_boot.js).

---

### Test 1: Full-Bed Chassis Squareness & Circle Roundness
* **Boundary & Center Inset:**
  * Enforces $X_{\min} = 5.0\text{mm}$, $X_{\max\text{eff}} = X_{\max} - 5.0\text{mm}$ (e.g. $595.0\text{mm}$ on a 600mm bed).
  * Enforces $Y_{\min} = 5.0\text{mm}$, $Y_{\max\text{eff}} = Y_{\max} - 5.0\text{mm}$ (e.g. $495.0\text{mm}$ on a 500mm bed).
  * Center intersection calculated at $(C_x, C_y) = (X_{\max}/2, Y_{\max}/2)$.
* **Diagonals Crossing at Center:**
  * **Diagonal 1:** $(X_{\min}, Y_{\min}) \to (X_{\max\text{eff}}, Y_{\max\text{eff}})$
  * **Diagonal 2:** $(X_{\min}, Y_{\max\text{eff}}) \to (X_{\max\text{eff}}, Y_{\min})$
  * Crossing point forms a precision center intersection.
* **5 Concentric Squares & Inscribed Tangent Circles:**
  * Mills 5 concentric squares in descending size ($1.0\times, 0.8\times, 0.6\times, 0.4\times, 0.2\times$) centered over the diagonal intersection.
  * Inscribes a tangent circle within each square, touching the midpoints of the 4 square sides ($r = \text{side}/2$).
* **Diagnostic Goal:**
  * **Chassis Squareness:** Measure Diagonal 1 vs. Diagonal 2 length with a steel tape/gauge. Equal lengths confirm $90^\circ$ orthogonality (no chassis rhomboid skew).
  * **Circle Roundness:** Measure X-axis vs. Y-axis diameter of each circle using calipers. Equal diameters verify zero backlash and correct $1:1$ steps/mm scaling.

---

### Test 2: 4-Quadrant 3D Relief & Stepped Cavity Test (120x120mm Stock)
* **Workpiece & Clamping Setup:**
  * $120.0\text{mm} \times 120.0\text{mm} \times 20.0\text{mm}$ workpiece mounted and clamped on a $20.0\text{mm}$ spoilboard (**$40.0\text{mm}$ total stack** from machine table).
  * WCS origin at lower-left, $Z = 0.0$ at the **workpiece top**.
  * Prominent clamping safety callout and 3D clamp visualization.
* **4 Quadrants:**
  * **Quad 1 (Top-Left): Inverted Stepped Cone Hole:**
    * $16.0\text{mm}$ total depth ($Z = 0 \to -16.0\text{mm}$ leaving a $4.0\text{mm}$ floor).
    * Concentric circular steps with $0.1\text{mm}$ Z increments and $1.0\text{mm}$ horizontal stepover ($\varnothing 48\text{mm}$ top $\to \varnothing 16\text{mm}$ bottom).
  * **Quad 2 (Top-Right): Inverted Stepped Square Pyramid Hole:**
    * $16.0\text{mm}$ total depth down to $Z = -16.0\text{mm}$ ($4.0\text{mm}$ floor).
    * Stepped square cavity ($48\times 48\text{mm}$ top $\to 16\times 16\text{mm}$ bottom).
  * **Quad 3 (Bottom-Left): Raised 3D Cone on 4mm ZFloor:**
    * Quadrant area hogged down to $Z = -16.0\text{mm}$ ($4.0\text{mm}$ remaining floor).
    * Freestanding raised cone rises $14\text{mm}$ tall from the $4\text{mm}$ floor up to the **$18.0\text{mm}$ peak** ($Z = -2.0\text{mm}$), with $0.1\text{mm}$ Z passes and $1.0\text{mm}$ X/Y stepover ($\varnothing 44\text{mm}$ base $\to \varnothing 6\text{mm}$ apex).
  * **Quad 4 (Bottom-Right): Raised 4-Sided Square Pyramid on 4mm ZFloor:**
    * Quadrant area hogged down to $4.0\text{mm}$ floor ($Z = -16.0\text{mm}$).
    * 4-sided square pyramid rises from $4.0\text{mm}$ floor up to the **$18.0\text{mm}$ peak** ($44\times 44\text{mm}$ base $\to 6\times 6\text{mm}$ peak with 4 crisp corner ridges).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# CLEJS Daily Upstream Tracking Script (JumpStart 3D & Vellum Vector Studio)
set -e

if (pwd -W) >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd -W)"
else
    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
fi

JS_ORIGINAL="$PROJECT_ROOT/JSoriginal/index.htm"
JS_DEV="$PROJECT_ROOT/Dev/index.htm"
JS_HISTORY="$PROJECT_ROOT/JSoriginal_history"

VV_ORIGINAL="$PROJECT_ROOT/VVSource/index.htm"
VV_DEV="$PROJECT_ROOT/Vellum/index.htm"
VV_HISTORY="$PROJECT_ROOT/VVSource_history"

REPORTS="$PROJECT_ROOT/upstream-reports"

mkdir -p "$JS_HISTORY" "$VV_HISTORY" "$REPORTS"

PYTHON_CMD="python"
if ! command -v python >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    PYTHON_CMD="python3"
fi

$PYTHON_CMD -c "
import urllib.request
import urllib.parse
import re
import hashlib
import os
import sys
from datetime import datetime

site_url = 'https://classyapps.org/'
req = urllib.request.Request(site_url, headers={'User-Agent': 'Mozilla/5.0'})
try:
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as resp:
        html = resp.read().decode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
except Exception as ex:
    print(f'[ERROR] Could not fetch {site_url}: {ex}')
    sys.exit(1)

def track_app(name, pattern, orig_path, hist_dir, dev_path, min_size=50000):
    matches = re.findall(pattern, html, re.I)
    if not matches:
        print(f'[ERROR] Could not find {name} download link on {site_url}.')
        return None
    
    app_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(site_url, matches[0])
    print(f'[CLEJS] Found upstream {name}: {app_url}')
    
    temp_file = os.path.join(r'$PROJECT_ROOT', f'.{name.lower()}_temp.htm')
    urllib.request.urlretrieve(app_url, temp_file)
    
    with open(temp_file, 'rb') as f:
        temp_bytes = f.read()
    
    if len(temp_bytes) < min_size:
        print(f'[ERROR] Downloaded {name} file is too small ({len(temp_bytes)} bytes).')
        if os.path.exists(temp_file):
            os.remove(temp_file)
        return None
        
    upstream_hash = hashlib.sha256(temp_bytes).hexdigest().upper()
    prev_hash = None
    prev_size = 0
    if os.path.exists(orig_path):
        with open(orig_path, 'rb') as f:
            prev_bytes = f.read()
        prev_hash = hashlib.sha256(prev_bytes).hexdigest().upper()
        prev_size = len(prev_bytes)
        
    changed = (upstream_hash != prev_hash)
    stamp = datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M%S')
    
    if changed:
        if prev_hash and os.path.exists(orig_path):
            backup_name = f'index-{stamp}-{prev_hash[:12]}.htm'
            backup_path = os.path.join(hist_dir, backup_name)
            os.replace(orig_path, backup_path)
            print(f'[CLEJS] Backed up prior {name} upstream to {backup_name}')
        os.replace(temp_file, orig_path)
        print(f'[CLEJS] Updated {orig_path} with latest release.')
    else:
        if os.path.exists(temp_file):
            os.remove(temp_file)
        print(f'[CLEJS] Upstream {name} is unchanged.')
        
    dev_hash = None
    dev_size = 0
    if os.path.exists(dev_path):
        with open(dev_path, 'rb') as f:
            dev_bytes = f.read()
        dev_hash = hashlib.sha256(dev_bytes).hexdigest().upper()
        dev_size = len(dev_bytes)
        
    dev_status = 'Identical to upstream' if dev_hash == upstream_hash else 'Customized / Different'
    upstream_status = 'Updated' if changed else 'No change'
    ver_m = re.search(r'v[\d.]+', app_url, re.I)
    version = ver_m.group(0) if ver_m else 'latest'
    
    return {
        'name': name,
        'app_url': app_url,
        'version': version,
        'upstream_status': upstream_status,
        'prev_hash': prev_hash,
        'prev_size': prev_size,
        'upstream_hash': upstream_hash,
        'upstream_size': len(temp_bytes),
        'dev_hash': dev_hash,
        'dev_size': dev_size,
        'dev_status': dev_status
    }

# 1. Track JumpStart 3D
js_info = track_app(
    'JumpStart_3D',
    r'href\s*=\s*[\"\']([^\"\']*jumpstart_3d_v[\d.]+\.htm)[\"\']',
    r'$JS_ORIGINAL',
    r'$JS_HISTORY',
    r'$JS_DEV',
    min_size=1000000
)

# 2. Track Vellum Vector Studio
vv_info = track_app(
    'Vellum_Vector_Studio',
    r'href\s*=\s*[\"\']([^\"\']*(?:Vellum_Vector_Studio|vellum)[^\"\']*\.htm)[\"\']',
    r'$VV_ORIGINAL',
    r'$VV_HISTORY',
    r'$VV_DEV',
    min_size=200000
)

today = datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
report_file = os.path.join(r'$REPORTS', f'{today}.md')

report_lines = [
    f'# ClassyApps Daily Upstream Check - {today}',
    '',
    f'- Source page: {site_url}',
    f'- Automated check tracks clean upstream releases daily for both JumpStart 3D and Vellum Vector Studio.',
    f'- Dev and Vellum working directories are never overwritten automatically.',
    ''
]

for info in [js_info, vv_info]:
    if not info:
        continue
    report_lines.extend([
        f'## {info[\"name\"]} (Upstream: {info[\"version\"]})',
        f'- App URL: {info[\"app_url\"]}',
        f'- Status vs previous pristine archive: **{info[\"upstream_status\"]}**',
        '',
        '| File | Previous Upstream SHA-256 | Prev size (bytes) | Current Upstream SHA-256 | Current size (bytes) | Workspace SHA-256 | Workspace size (bytes) | Upstream vs Workspace |',
        '|---|---|---:|---|---:|---|---:|---|',
        f'| index.htm | {info[\"prev_hash\"] or \"None\"} | {info[\"prev_size\"]} | {info[\"upstream_hash\"]} | {info[\"upstream_size\"]} | {info[\"dev_hash\"] or \"None\"} | {info[\"dev_size\"]} | {info[\"dev_status\"]} |',
        ''
    ])

with open(report_file, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    f.write('\\n'.join(report_lines))

print(f'[CLEJS] Daily upstream report written to: {report_file}')
"

    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as resp:
        html = resp.read().decode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
except Exception as ex:
    print(f'[ERROR] Could not fetch {site_url}: {ex}')
    sys.exit(1)

def track_app(name, pattern, orig_path, hist_dir, dev_path, min_size=50000):
    matches = re.findall(pattern, html, re.I)
    if not matches:
        print(f'[ERROR] Could not find {name} download link on {site_url}.')
        return None
    
    app_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(site_url, matches[0])
    print(f'[CLEJS] Found upstream {name}: {app_url}')
    
    temp_file = os.path.join(r'$PROJECT_ROOT', f'.{name.lower()}_temp.htm')
    urllib.request.urlretrieve(app_url, temp_file)
    
    with open(temp_file, 'rb') as f:
        temp_bytes = f.read()
    
    if len(temp_bytes) < min_size:
        print(f'[ERROR] Downloaded {name} file is too small ({len(temp_bytes)} bytes).')
        if os.path.exists(temp_file):
            os.remove(temp_file)
        return None
        
    upstream_hash = hashlib.sha256(temp_bytes).hexdigest().upper()
    prev_hash = None
    prev_size = 0
    if os.path.exists(orig_path):
        with open(orig_path, 'rb') as f:
            prev_bytes = f.read()
        prev_hash = hashlib.sha256(prev_bytes).hexdigest().upper()
        prev_size = len(prev_bytes)
        
    changed = (upstream_hash != prev_hash)
    stamp = datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M%S')
    
    if changed:
        if prev_hash and os.path.exists(orig_path):
            backup_name = f'index-{stamp}-{prev_hash[:12]}.htm'
            backup_path = os.path.join(hist_dir, backup_name)
            os.replace(orig_path, backup_path)
            print(f'[CLEJS] Backed up prior {name} upstream to {backup_name}')
        os.replace(temp_file, orig_path)
        print(f'[CLEJS] Updated {orig_path} with latest release.')
    else:
        if os.path.exists(temp_file):
            os.remove(temp_file)
        print(f'[CLEJS] Upstream {name} is unchanged.')
        
    dev_hash = None
    dev_size = 0
    if os.path.exists(dev_path):
        with open(dev_path, 'rb') as f:
            dev_bytes = f.read()
        dev_hash = hashlib.sha256(dev_bytes).hexdigest().upper()
        dev_size = len(dev_bytes)
        
    dev_status = 'Identical to upstream' if dev_hash == upstream_hash else 'Customized / Different'
    upstream_status = 'Updated' if changed else 'No change'
    ver_m = re.search(r'v[\d.]+', app_url, re.I)
    version = ver_m.group(0) if ver_m else 'latest'
    
    return {
        'name': name,
        'app_url': app_url,
        'version': version,
        'upstream_status': upstream_status,
        'prev_hash': prev_hash,
        'prev_size': prev_size,
        'upstream_hash': upstream_hash,
        'upstream_size': len(temp_bytes),
        'dev_hash': dev_hash,
        'dev_size': dev_size,
        'dev_status': dev_status
    }

# 1. Track JumpStart 3D
js_info = track_app(
    'JumpStart_3D',
    r'href\s*=\s*[\"\']([^\"\']*jumpstart_3d_v[\d.]+\.htm)[\"\']',
    r'$JS_ORIGINAL',
    r'$JS_HISTORY',

)

# 2. Track Vellum Vector Studio

    r'$VV_ORIGINAL',
    r'$VV_HISTORY',
    r'$VV_DEV',
    min_size=200000
)

today = datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
report_file = os.path.join(r'$REPORTS', f'{today}.md')

report_lines = [
    f'# ClassyApps Daily Upstream Check - {today}',
    '',
    f'- Source page: {site_url}',
    f'- Automated check tracks clean upstream releases daily for both JumpStart 3D and Vellum Vector Studio.',
    f'- Dev and Vellum working directories are never overwritten automatically.',

]

for info in [js_info, vv_info]:
    if not info:

    report_lines.extend([

with open(report_file, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:

import re
import math

def parse_svg_to_jumpstart_entities(svg_str):
    # Regex to find <rect>, <circle>, <line>, and <path>
    pts = []
    ents = []
    pt_map = {}
    
    def add_pt(x, y):
        k = f"{round(x, 4)},{round(y, 4)}"
        if k in pt_map:
            return pt_map[k]
        pid = f"p_{len(pts)+1}"
        pts.append({"id": pid, "x": round(x, 4), "y": round(y, 4)})
        pt_map[k] = pid
        return pid

    # 1. Rectangles: <rect x=".." y=".." width=".." height=".."/>
    for m in re.finditer(r'<rect\s+([^>]+)/?>', svg_str):
        attrs = dict(re.findall(r'(\w+)=["\']([^"\']+)["\']', m.group(1)))
        x = float(attrs.get('x', 0))
        y = -float(attrs.get('y', 0)) # flip SVG Y to CAD Y
        w = float(attrs.get('width', 0))
        h = float(attrs.get('height', 0))
        p1 = add_pt(x, y)
        p2 = add_pt(x + w, y)
        p3 = add_pt(x + w, y - h)
        p4 = add_pt(x, y - h)
        ents.append({"id": f"e_{len(ents)+1}", "t": "line", "a": p1, "b": p2})
        ents.append({"id": f"e_{len(ents)+1}", "t": "line", "a": p2, "b": p3})
        ents.append({"id": f"e_{len(ents)+1}", "t": "line", "a": p3, "b": p4})
        ents.append({"id": f"e_{len(ents)+1}", "t": "line", "a": p4, "b": p1})

    # 2. Circles: <circle cx=".." cy=".." r=".."/>
    for m in re.finditer(r'<circle\s+([^>]+)/?>', svg_str):
        attrs = dict(re.findall(r'(\w+)=["\']([^"\']+)["\']', m.group(1)))
        cx = float(attrs.get('cx', 0))
        cy = -float(attrs.get('cy', 0))
        r = float(attrs.get('r', 0))
        c = add_pt(cx, cy)
        ents.append({"id": f"e_{len(ents)+1}", "t": "circle", "c": c, "r": r})

    return pts, ents

svg_sample = '''<svg viewBox="0 0 100 100">
  <rect x="10" y="10" width="80" height="80"/>
  <circle cx="50" cy="50" r="15"/>
</svg>'''

pts, ents = parse_svg_to_jumpstart_entities(svg_sample)
print("Points count:", len(pts), "Ents count:", len(ents))
print("Ents:", ents)

### Vellum Vector Studio Integration Complete

**Vellum Vector Studio** is fully integrated alongside **JumpStart 3D** and **CLE** in our customized JumpStart 3D suite, with dual transfer options (**2D Sketch** and **Direct 3D Extrusion**) and automated upstream daily release tracking.

---

### What Was Built & Configured

```
├── VVSource/                         # Pristine upstream releases from classyapps.org
│   └── index.htm                     # Clean upstream Vellum Vector Studio v1.6
├── VVSource_history/                 # Archive of past versions (v1.5 and v1.6 timestamped + SHA-256)
├── Vellum/                           # Integrated application folder
│   └── index.htm                     # Vellum app with "Save to JS Workspace" toolbar & modal bridge
├── update_jumpstart.sh               # Dual daily tracking script (JumpStart 3D + Vellum Vector Studio)
├── upstream-reports/                 # Unified daily reports comparing upstream vs workspace
└── Dev/
    ├── cle_tools/
    │   ├── cle_vellum.js             # Vellum bridge module (postMessage receiver & CAD entity converter)
    │   ├── cle_boot.js               # "Vector Studio" button added to CLE ribbon
    │   └── cle_bundle.js             # Rebuilt bundle including cle_vellum.js
    └── index.htm                     # Added "Vector Studio" workspace tab to wstabs & window.Se manager
```

---

### How to Use

1. **Launch Vector Studio:**
   - Click the **`Vector Studio`** tab in the JumpStart workspace tabs ([`wstabs`](file:///d:/CLEJS/Dev/index.htm#L5683)), or click the **`Vector Studio`** button in the CLE ribbon.
   - A full-screen drawer opens displaying Vellum Vector Studio with its complete suite of tools: box maker, text on path, shape drawing, autotrace, and laser/vinyl kerf previews.

2. **Send Drawing to JumpStart 3D Workspace:**
   - Click the blue **`Save to JS Workspace`** button in Vellum's top toolbar (or choose it from the **Export** menu).
   - An export dialog lets you choose between two modes:
     - **Option A (2D Editable Sketch):** Imports vector curves onto your chosen workplane (XY, XZ, or YZ). Closed outlines shade blue, remaining fully editable for dimensions, constraints, or manual extrusion.
     - **Option B (Direct 3D Extruded Body):** Creates a 3D solid CAD body directly with your specified extrusion thickness (e.g. 5.0 mm), instantly rendering in the 3D viewport, timeline, and body tree.
   - Click **Send to JumpStart 3D**; the Vellum modal closes and the 3D viewport immediately displays your new sketch or solid part.

3. **Daily Upstream Tracking:**
   - Running `bash update_jumpstart.sh` automatically checks `https://classyapps.org/` for new versions of **both** JumpStart 3D and Vellum Vector Studio.
   - New upstream releases are downloaded to [`JSoriginal/`](file:///d:/CLEJS/JSoriginal) and [`VVSource/`](file:///d:/CLEJS/VVSource), previous versions are archived into history with SHA-256 signatures, and a report is logged in [`upstream-reports/`](file:///d:/CLEJS/upstream-reports/). Dev and Vellum workspaces remain protected and are never overwritten.

### Why the PNG Didn't Paste to the Workspace

When you opened the `.png` in Vellum, it loaded as a **raster image** (pixels) rather than **vector paths** (lines, arcs, curves). 

Our initial bridge was looking strictly for vector path segments to convert into 2D CAD sketch curves and 3D solid extrusions. Because a raw PNG has no vector paths yet, the bridge bypassed it.

---

### Two Ways We Can Handle PNGs Between Vellum & JumpStart

#### 1. Native Workplane Picture (Reference Image in 3D)
JumpStart 3D has a native picture feature (`sketch.image`). 
- When you send a raw PNG from Vellum to JumpStart, the bridge can place the PNG directly onto the JumpStart workplane/bed with a translucent background.
- You can position it, scale it, and use it as a visual reference in the 3D scene.

#### 2. Vectorize / Autotrace First (Cut-Ready 3D Solid or Sketch)
Because CNC spindles and laser cutters follow vector paths (not pixels):
- In Vellum Vector Studio, there is a built-in **Trace / Autotrace** button in the toolbar.
- Clicking **Trace** in Vellum converts the PNG's outlines into vector curves.
- Once traced, clicking **Save to JS Workspace** will convert those curves into:
  - An **Editable 2D Sketch** (Option A), or
  - A **3D Solid Extrusion** (Option B) rising up from the bed.

---

### Proposed Solution

We can support **both** workflows seamlessly:

1. **If Vellum has a raw PNG image:**
   The bridge transfers the PNG directly onto the JumpStart 3D workplane so it appears in the 3D scene immediately as a reference image, and alerts you that it's a reference image.
2. **If you trace the PNG in Vellum:**
   The bridge transfers the traced vector contours as an editable sketch or 3D solid extrusion.

Would you like me to enable the bridge to import raw PNG/JPG images directly onto the JumpStart workplane as reference pictures?
thinking:
JumpStart 3D allows attaching a background image to a sketch via the `sketch.image` property. This property holds details like the image source, name, dimensions, and initial transformation values, which is then rendered directly onto the viewport.


The user likely opened the PNG to either vectorize it using AutoTrace, or to directly import the image into JumpStart for tracing on the workplane. The current data bridge only handles vector data with `segments`, and the image object has `type: 'image'` without `segments`. Consequently, the image was silently skipped during the data transfer.

### Direct PNG & Bitmap Image Support Added

We have updated both the **Vellum Vector Studio export dialog** and the **JumpStart 3D bridge** to natively handle `.png`, `.jpg`, and bitmap images:

---

### What Has Been Implemented

1. **Automatic Image Detection in Vellum:**
   - When you open or place a PNG/JPG in Vellum, the export modal now automatically detects it and surfaces:
     - **Option: Workplane Reference Picture (3D Canvas)** (auto-selected when you have an image loaded).
     - **Tip Banner:** Explains that you can also click **Trace** in Vellum's toolbar if you want to turn the image into cut-ready 3D vector paths/extrusions.

2. **Native 3D Workplane Placement in JumpStart:**
   - Clicking **Send to JumpStart 3D** now transfers the PNG directly onto the JumpStart 3D workplane (`sketch.image`).
   - The image renders directly in the 3D scene on the machine bed with transparency, allowing you to view it, scale it, and trace or model over it in 3D.

3. **Combined Images & Vectors:**
   - If you trace the PNG in Vellum or draw vector shapes over it, clicking **Send to JumpStart 3D** transfers **both**: the vector curves (as an editable sketch or 3D solid) **plus** the background image aligned underneath it!

---

### Ready to Test in Browser

1. Refresh [`Dev/index.htm`](file:///d:/CLEJS/Dev/index.htm) in your browser.
2. Click **`Vector Studio`** tab on the left (or in the CLE Ribbon).
3. Open your `.png` file in Vellum.
4. Click **`Save to JS Workspace`**:
   - To view the PNG on the bed: Click **Send to JumpStart 3D** (the image is placed directly on the 3D workplane).
   - To make it a solid 3D part: In Vellum, select the image, click **Trace** to convert it into vector contours, then click **Save to JS Workspace** $\to$ **3D Extruded Body** $\to$ **Send to JumpStart 3D**!

from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

with sync_playwright() as p:
    browser = p.chromium.launch(
        headless=True,
        args=["--allow-file-access-from-files", "--disable-web-security"]
    )
    page = browser.new_page()
    page.goto("file:///D:/CLEJS/Dev/index.htm")
    page.wait_for_timeout(3500)

    # Collect console logs
    console_logs = []
    page.on("console", lambda msg: console_logs.append(f"[{msg.type}] {msg.text}"))

    # 1. Switch to CLE tab
    page.click("#ws-cle")
    page.wait_for_timeout(500)

    # 2. Click Vector Studio ribbon button
    page.click("#cle-r-vellum")
    page.wait_for_timeout(1000)

    # Check if iframe loaded
    iframe_handle = page.query_selector("#cle-vellum-iframe")
    print("Iframe handle found:", bool(iframe_handle))
    frame = page.frame(name="cle-vellum-iframe") or iframe_handle.content_frame()
    print("Frame found:", bool(frame))

    # In Vellum iframe, check what buttons exist
    btn_save = frame.query_selector("#btnSaveToJS")
    print("btnSaveToJS found in iframe:", bool(btn_save))

    # Add a rectangle or shape in Vellum
    frame.evaluate("""() => {
        // Create a simple box in Vellum
        const rect = {
            id: 'o_test_rect',
            type: 'path',
            closed: true,
            angle: 0,
            fill: '#38bdf8',
            stroke: '#0284c7',
            strokeWidth: 2,
            visible: true,
            segments: [
                { type: 'M', x: 50, y: 50 },
                { type: 'L', x: 150, y: 50 },
                { type: 'L', x: 150, y: 150 },
                { type: 'L', x: 50, y: 150 },
                { type: 'Z' }
            ]
        };
        if (typeof state !== 'undefined' && state.objects) {
            state.objects.push(rect);
        }
    }""")

    # Click btnSaveToJS to open modal
    frame.click("#btnSaveToJS")
    page.wait_for_timeout(500)

    modal_vis = frame.is_visible("#jsExportModal")
    print("jsExportModal visible:", modal_vis)

    # Test Option 1: 2D Sketch
    frame.click("#optModeSketch")
    page.wait_for_timeout(200)

    # Click confirm
    frame.click("#confirmJsModalBtn")
    page.wait_for_timeout(1500)

    # Now check state in parent window!
    parent_state = page.evaluate("""() => {
        const modal = document.getElementById('cle-vellum-modal');
        const doc = window.Se ? window.Se.doc : null;
        const app = window.app || window.xe;
        return {
            modalDisplay: modal ? modal.style.display : null,
            sketcherActive: app ? !!app.sketcher?.active : false,
            sketchesCount: doc ? doc.sketches.length : 0,
            lastSketch: doc && doc.sketches.length ? doc.sketches[doc.sketches.length - 1] : null,
            bodiesCount: doc ? doc.bodies.length : 0
        };
    }""")
    print("Parent state after Option 1 (Sketch):", parent_state)

    print("\nRecent console logs:")
    for log in console_logs[-15:]:
        print(log)

    browser.close()

### Root Cause Identified & Resolved

1. **State Isolation in Vellum (`Vellum/index.htm`):**
   - Vellum's core engine was enclosed inside a private closure IIFE `(function(){ "use strict"; const state = ... })();`.
   - The export bridge script was in a separate script tag and evaluated `typeof state !== 'undefined'` as `false`. This resulted in `state.objects` always returning an empty array `[]` regardless of what was drawn or opened on screen.
   - **Fix:** Exposed `window.Vellum = { state, objects, getExportSvg, ... }` from within the main closure so all drawn shapes, text, and images are directly accessible by the export bridge.

2. **2D Sketch Editor Trapping (`Dev/cle_tools/cle_vellum.js`):**
   - On import, `app.enterSketch(skId)` was being triggered. This switched JumpStart into the 2D sketcher, which temporarily dimms/hides the 3D machine bed, spoilboard, and CLE tools.
   - **Fix:** Removed `app.enterSketch(skId)`. The transferred sketch or body is now placed directly in the 3D scene (`sketchViews`) on top of the spoilboard at $(X=300\,\text{mm},\, Y=250\,\text{mm},\, Z=20.10\,\text{mm})$.

3. **Solid Extrusion Profile Matching:**
   - JumpStart's kernel requires topological profile keys (e.g. `e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3`) and interior sample points to generate 3D solids.
   - **Fix:** Exposed `window.Ei` in `Dev/index.htm` and integrated it into `cle_vellum.js` so closed vector contours from Vellum are immediately matched and converted into native 3D bodies.

4. **Return & Navigation:**
   - When **"Save to JS Workspace"** is clicked, Vellum now:
     1. Exports the chosen mode (2D Sketch, 3D Body, or Raster Picture).
     2. Closes the Vellum modal view.
     3. Returns to the active workspace (**CLE** or **Design**).
     4. Positions and auto-fits the camera directly at the center of the spoilboard.

import asyncio
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

async def run():
    async with async_playwright() as p:
        browser = await p.chromium.launch(headless=True)
        context = await browser.new_context(viewport={"width": 1400, "height": 900})
        page = await context.new_page()

        print("[TEST] Navigating to http://127.0.0.1:8001/Dev/index.htm...")
        await page.goto("http://127.0.0.1:8001/Dev/index.htm", timeout=30000)
        await page.wait_for_timeout(3000)

        # 1. Switch to CLE tab
        print("[TEST] Switching to CLE tab...")
        await page.click("#tab-cle")
        await page.wait_for_timeout(1000)

        # 2. Check Grayscale 3D button in ribbon
        print("[TEST] Checking for '#cle-r-grayscale' ribbon button...")
        gray_btn = await page.wait_for_selector("#cle-r-grayscale", timeout=5000)
        assert gray_btn is not None, "Ribbon button '#cle-r-grayscale' not found!"
        print("  [OK] Ribbon button '#cle-r-grayscale' exists.")

        # 3. Click '#cle-r-grayscale' to open modal
        print("[TEST] Clicking '#cle-r-grayscale' to open modal...")
        await gray_btn.click()
        await page.wait_for_timeout(1000)

        modal = await page.wait_for_selector("#cle-active-modal", timeout=5000)
        assert modal is not None, "Active modal not found!"

        # Check that Grayscale tab and panel are active
        gray_panel = await page.wait_for_selector("#cle-slicer-panel-gray", timeout=5000)
        is_visible = await gray_panel.is_visible()
        assert is_visible, "Grayscale panel should be visible when opened via #cle-r-grayscale!"
        print("  [OK] Grayscale panel is visible.")

        # Check preview canvas
        canvas = await page.wait_for_selector("#cle-gray-preview-canvas", timeout=5000)
        assert canvas is not None, "Preview canvas not found!"
        print("  [OK] Preview canvas rendered.")

        # 4. Test Tab Switching to CAD slicer and back
        print("[TEST] Testing tab switching...")
        await page.click("#cle-slicer-tab-cad")
        await page.wait_for_timeout(300)
        cad_visible = await page.is_visible("#cle-slicer-panel-cad")
        gray_visible = await page.is_visible("#cle-slicer-panel-gray")
        assert cad_visible and not gray_visible, "CAD panel should be visible, Gray hidden!"

        await page.click("#cle-slicer-tab-gray")
        await page.wait_for_timeout(300)
        cad_visible = await page.is_visible("#cle-slicer-panel-cad")
        gray_visible = await page.is_visible("#cle-slicer-panel-gray")
        assert gray_visible and not cad_visible, "Gray panel should be visible, CAD hidden!"
        print("  [OK] Tab switching works smoothly.")

        # 5. Test 'Create 3D Object in Workspace'
        print("[TEST] Testing 'Create 3D Object in Workspace' button...")
        create_btn = await page.wait_for_selector("#cle-gray-create-3d-btn", timeout=5000)
        await create_btn.click()
        await page.wait_for_timeout(2000)

        # Verify modal closed
        modal_closed = not await page.is_visible("#cle-active-modal")
        assert modal_closed, "Modal should close after creating 3D object!"
        print("  [OK] Modal closed.")

        # Verify 3D relief mesh created in scene at bed center
        mesh_info = await page.evaluate('''() => {
            const slicer = window.CLE?.slicer;
            const mesh = slicer?.reliefMesh;
            if (!mesh) return null;
            return {
                name: mesh.name,
                position: { x: mesh.position.x, y: mesh.position.y, z: mesh.position.z },
                vertexCount: mesh.geometry.attributes.position.count,
                indexCount: mesh.geometry.index.count
            };
        }''')
        print("  [RELIEF MESH INFO]:", mesh_info)
        assert mesh_info is not None, "Relief mesh not found on slicer!"
        assert mesh_info["position"]["x"] == 300.0, f"Expected X=300, got {mesh_info['position']['x']}"
        assert mesh_info["position"]["y"] == 250.0, f"Expected Y=250, got {mesh_info['position']['y']}"
        assert abs(mesh_info["position"]["z"] - 20.10) < 0.01, f"Expected Z=20.10, got {mesh_info['position']['z']}"
        assert mesh_info["vertexCount"] > 1000, f"Expected >1000 vertices, got {mesh_info['vertexCount']}"
        print("  [OK] 3D Relief mesh generated at bed center (300, 250, 20.10) with solid geometry!")

        # 6. Test 'Slice to Continuous Z'
        print("[TEST] Re-opening modal and testing 'Slice to Continuous Z'...")
        await page.click("#tab-cle")
        await page.click("#cle-r-grayscale")
        await page.wait_for_timeout(1000)

        slice_btn = await page.wait_for_selector("#cle-gray-slice-run-btn", timeout=5000)
        await slice_btn.click()
        await page.wait_for_timeout(2000)

        # Check slices in scene and HUD mounted
        slice_info = await page.evaluate('''() => {
            const slicer = window.CLE?.slicer;
            return {
                layerCount: slicer?.slicedLayers?.length || 0,
                hasGCode: !!slicer?.rawGCode && slicer.rawGCode.length > 50,
                gcodePreview: slicer?.rawGCode?.split('\\n').slice(0, 5).join('; ')
            };
        }''')
        print("  [SLICE INFO]:", slice_info)
        assert slice_info["layerCount"] > 0, "No slices generated!"
        assert slice_info["hasGCode"], "No G-code generated!"

        hud = await page.wait_for_selector("#cle-slicer-hud", timeout=5000)
        assert hud is not None, "Slicer HUD not mounted!"
        print("  [OK] Continuous Z slices generated, G-code built, and HUD mounted!")

        await page.screenshot(path="scratch/grayscale_relief_verified.png")
        print("[TEST] All Grayscale 3D tests PASSED! Screenshot saved to scratch/grayscale_relief_verified.png")
        await browser.close()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(run())

from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

def run():
    with sync_playwright() as p:
        browser = p.chromium.launch(
            headless=True,
            args=["--allow-file-access-from-files", "--disable-web-security"]
        )
        page = browser.new_page(viewport={"width": 1400, "height": 900})

        print("[TEST] Navigating to file:///D:/CLEJS/Dev/index.htm...")
        page.goto("file:///D:/CLEJS/Dev/index.htm")
        page.wait_for_timeout(3500)

        # Set to Advanced mode
        page.evaluate("""() => {
            const app = window.app || window.xe;
            if (app && app.setMode) app.setMode('advanced');
        }""")
        page.wait_for_timeout(1000)

        # 1. Switch to CLE tab
        print("[TEST] Switching to CLE tab...")
        page.click("#ws-cle")
        page.wait_for_timeout(1000)

        # 2. Check Grayscale 3D button in ribbon
        print("[TEST] Checking for '#cle-r-grayscale' ribbon button...")
        gray_btn = page.wait_for_selector("#cle-r-grayscale", timeout=5000)
        assert gray_btn is not None, "Ribbon button '#cle-r-grayscale' not found!"
        print("  [OK] Ribbon button '#cle-r-grayscale' exists.")

        # 3. Click '#cle-r-grayscale' to open modal
        print("[TEST] Clicking '#cle-r-grayscale' to open modal...")
        gray_btn.click()
        page.wait_for_timeout(1000)

        modal = page.wait_for_selector("#cle-active-modal", timeout=5000)
        assert modal is not None, "Active modal not found!"

        # Check that Grayscale tab and panel are active
        gray_panel = page.wait_for_selector("#cle-slicer-panel-gray", timeout=5000)
        is_visible = gray_panel.is_visible()
        assert is_visible, "Grayscale panel should be visible when opened via #cle-r-grayscale!"
        print("  [OK] Grayscale panel is visible.")

        # Check preview canvas
        canvas = page.wait_for_selector("#cle-gray-preview-canvas", timeout=5000)
        assert canvas is not None, "Preview canvas not found!"
        print("  [OK] Preview canvas rendered.")

        # 4. Test Tab Switching to CAD slicer and back
        print("[TEST] Testing tab switching...")
        page.click("#cle-slicer-tab-cad")
        page.wait_for_timeout(400)
        cad_visible = page.is_visible("#cle-slicer-panel-cad")
        gray_visible = page.is_visible("#cle-slicer-panel-gray")
        assert cad_visible and not gray_visible, "CAD panel should be visible, Gray hidden!"

        page.click("#cle-slicer-tab-gray")
        page.wait_for_timeout(400)
        cad_visible = page.is_visible("#cle-slicer-panel-cad")
        gray_visible = page.is_visible("#cle-slicer-panel-gray")
        assert gray_visible and not cad_visible, "Gray panel should be visible, CAD hidden!"
        print("  [OK] Tab switching works smoothly.")

        # 5. Test 'Create 3D Object in Workspace'
        print("[TEST] Testing 'Create 3D Object in Workspace' button...")
        create_btn = page.wait_for_selector("#cle-gray-create-3d-btn", timeout=5000)
        create_btn.click()
        page.wait_for_timeout(2000)

        # Verify modal closed
        modal_closed = not page.is_visible("#cle-active-modal")
        assert modal_closed, "Modal should close after creating 3D object!"
        print("  [OK] Modal closed.")

        # Verify 3D relief mesh created in scene at bed center
        mesh_info = page.evaluate('''() => {
            const slicer = window.CLE?.slicer;
            const mesh = slicer?.reliefMesh;
            if (!mesh) return null;
            return {
                name: mesh.name,
                position: { x: mesh.position.x, y: mesh.position.y, z: mesh.position.z },
                vertexCount: mesh.geometry.attributes.position.count,
                indexCount: mesh.geometry.index.count
            };
        }''')
        print("  [RELIEF MESH INFO]:", mesh_info)
        assert mesh_info is not None, "Relief mesh not found on slicer!"
        assert mesh_info["position"]["x"] == 300.0, f"Expected X=300, got {mesh_info['position']['x']}"
        assert mesh_info["position"]["y"] == 250.0, f"Expected Y=250, got {mesh_info['position']['y']}"
        assert abs(mesh_info["position"]["z"] - 20.10) < 0.01, f"Expected Z=20.10, got {mesh_info['position']['z']}"
        assert mesh_info["vertexCount"] > 1000, f"Expected >1000 vertices, got {mesh_info['vertexCount']}"
        print("  [OK] 3D Relief mesh generated at bed center (300, 250, 20.10) with solid geometry!")

        # 6. Test 'Slice to Continuous Z'
        print("[TEST] Re-opening modal and testing 'Slice to Continuous Z'...")
        page.click("#ws-cle")
        page.wait_for_timeout(500)
        page.click("#cle-r-grayscale")
        page.wait_for_timeout(1000)

        slice_btn = page.wait_for_selector("#cle-gray-slice-run-btn", timeout=5000)
        slice_btn.click()
        page.wait_for_timeout(2000)

        # Check slices in scene and HUD mounted
        slice_info = page.evaluate('''() => {
            const slicer = window.CLE?.slicer;
            return {
                layerCount: slicer?.slicedLayers?.length || 0,
                hasGCode: !!slicer?.rawGCode && slicer.rawGCode.length > 50,
                gcodePreview: slicer?.rawGCode?.split('\\n').slice(0, 5).join('; ')
            };
        }''')
        print("  [SLICE INFO]:", slice_info)
        assert slice_info["layerCount"] > 0, "No slices generated!"
        assert slice_info["hasGCode"], "No G-code generated!"

        hud = page.wait_for_selector("#cle-slicer-hud", timeout=5000)
        assert hud is not None, "Slicer HUD not mounted!"
        print("  [OK] Continuous Z slices generated, G-code built, and HUD mounted!")

        page.screenshot(path="scratch/grayscale_relief_verified.png")
        print("[TEST] All Grayscale 3D tests PASSED! Screenshot saved to scratch/grayscale_relief_verified.png")
        browser.close()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    run()

The image is present, but the user cannot select it for slicing in either environment. The immediate hypothesis is an import issue where the image data is loaded but lacks the necessary attributes for interactive manipulation within these systems. Checking how images imported from VV behave compared to those created natively within JS/CLE is the next step. If native images are selectable, the problem is likely in how VV exports/imports.

CLE currently lacks interactive bed positioning for all object types. The absence of a direct 3D mouse gizmo in CLE limits user interaction, requiring a "move" command or transform input.

### Architectural Proposal: Plan 1 & Plan 2

Here is the detailed architectural breakdown and discussion for both plans before we start execution.

---

### **Plan 1: End-User Application Installer (`JSVCLE_Experimental<build_number>.exe`)**

#### 1. Components to Package
The installer will produce a self-contained executable in `dist/` containing:
1. **JumpStart 3D CAD (`Dev/`)**:
   - Complete JumpStart 3D core application with the CLEJS universal hook.
   - Fully compiled and validated `Dev/cle_tools/cle_bundle.js` and `cle_theme.css`.
   - Ribbon, real-time DRO, Slicer, Rotary chuck/live center, Calibration, Tool Library, Job Recovery, and Bed Object Positioner.
2. **Vellum Vector Studio (`Vellum/`)**:
   - Vellum Vector Studio v1.6 integrated with the bi-directional bridge (`window.Vellum`).
   - SVG export, 3D profile extrusion detector (`Ei`), and photo/image transfer directly to the JumpStart spoilboard center.
3. **Local Background Services (`tools/`)**:
   - `tools/CLE_server.py`: Local REST/WebSocket service on port `8765` handling Git Vault sync, SD card uploads, hardware telemetry, and PrusaSlicer CLI execution.
4. **Machine Vault (`vault/`)**:
   - Default machine profiles (TwoTrees TTC6050, TTC450, Laser, Custom), tool library definitions, spoilboard defaults, and recovery logs.
5. **Pristine Upstream Anchors**:
   - `JSoriginal/` and `VVSource/` with daily tracker scripts (`update_jumpstart.sh`).
6. **Launcher & Desktop Integration**:
   - Enhanced `cle_start.bat` (or a silent launcher executable) that starts `CLE_server.py` in the background and opens JumpStart 3D in standalone app mode (or default browser).
   - Desktop and Start Menu shortcuts labeled **JSVCLE Studio**.

#### 2. Key Design Questions for Plan 1:
- **Build Numbering:** Recommend using `git rev-list --count HEAD` or a timestamped format, for example: `JSVCLE_Experimental_b66.exe` (or `JSVCLE_Experimental_v1.0.66.exe`).
- **Python on the 2nd System:** Does your 2nd test system already have Python installed, or should the installer bundle a lightweight **Windows Embedded Python 3** (~15 MB) into `tools/python/` so `CLE_server.py` runs out of the box with zero manual dependencies? *(Recommended: bundle embedded Python for a 100% turnkey experience).*
- **Default Install Directory:** Currently set to `D:\CLEJS` with user-selectable path (e.g. `C:\Program Files\JSVCLE` or `C:\JSVCLE`).

---

### **Plan 2: Community GitHub Export & Developer Environment (`DevInstaller`)**

#### 1. Community GitHub Export Bundle
- **Repository Sanitization:**
  - Create an export script (`tools/export_github.py`) that exports the clean source tree for community publishing.
  - Sanitizes local tokens, personal machine paths, and excludes ephemeral files (`scratch/`, local test screenshots, `.system_generated/`, large binaries).
  - Generates community documentation:
    - `README.md`: Project overview, features, quick start, installation, architecture diagram.
    - `LICENSE`: Open-source license (e.g. MIT / Apache 2.0).
    - `CONTRIBUTING.md`: Guidelines for community contributions.
    - `.gitignore`: Proper exclusions for node_modules, Python venvs, dist builds, and cache.
- **Git Remote Target:**
  - Support setting the community remote URL (e.g. `git remote add community <github-url>`).

#### 2. Developer Toolchain Installer (`DevInstaller`)
- A standalone script (`tools/DevInstaller.ps1` / `DevInstaller.py`) that sets up any new developer machine in one pass:
  1. **Node.js**: Checks for Node/npm (needed for `bundle_cle.py` and syntax validation).
  2. **Python & Virtualenv**: Installs runtime requirements (`requests`, `playwright`, `pyserial`).
  3. **Inno Setup 6 (`iscc`)**: Installs Inno Setup via `winget install JRSoftware.InnoSetup` (or downloads the portable Inno compiler into `tools/iscc/`) so any developer can compile the `.exe` installer.
  4. **PrusaSlicer CLI**: Downloads and places portable PrusaSlicer into `tools/PrusaSlicer/`.
  5. **Playwright Browsers**: Runs `playwright install chromium` for automated E2E testing.

#### 3. Master Build & Tree Validation Script (`build_full_tree.sh` / `Build-FullTree.ps1`)
A single command that automates the full development lifecycle:
1. **Sync Upstream:** Runs `update_jumpstart.sh` to check `classyapps.org` for JS and VV updates.
2. **Compile Bundle:** Runs `bundle_cle.py` to produce `cle_bundle.js`.
3. **Run Test Suites:**
   - Syntax and build tests (`tools/test_build.sh`).
   - Playwright end-to-end tests (Vellum export, Bed manager, Grayscale 3D, Rotary Chuck, Slicer).
4. **GitHub Validation:** Runs `git fetch` and validates tree parity against the community GitHub repo.
5. **Installer Generation:** Invokes Inno Setup (`ISCC.exe`) to compile `dist/JSVCLE_Experimental<build_number>.exe`.

---

import subprocess
import time
import urllib.request
import json
from pathlib import Path

sandbox = Path("D:/CLEJS/test_install_sandbox")
python_exe = sandbox / "tools" / "python_runtime" / "python.exe"
server_py = sandbox / "tools" / "CLE_server.py"

print("[TEST] Checking sandbox files...")
assert (sandbox / "Dev" / "index.htm").exists(), "Dev/index.htm missing in sandbox!"
assert (sandbox / "Vellum" / "index.htm").exists(), "Vellum/index.htm missing in sandbox!"
assert (sandbox / "cle_start.bat").exists(), "cle_start.bat missing in sandbox!"
assert (sandbox / "cle_server_start.bat").exists(), "cle_server_start.bat missing in sandbox!"
assert (sandbox / "vellum_start.bat").exists(), "vellum_start.bat missing in sandbox!"
assert python_exe.exists(), "Embedded python missing in sandbox!"
assert server_py.exists(), "CLE_server.py missing in sandbox!"
print("  [OK] All files verified in test sandbox.")

print("[TEST] Launching CLE_server from sandbox...")
proc = subprocess.Popen([str(python_exe), str(server_py)], cwd=str(sandbox))
time.sleep(2)

try:
    with urllib.request.urlopen("http://127.0.0.1:8765/api/status", timeout=5) as resp:
        data = json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))
        print("  [SERVER RESPONSE]:", data)
        assert data.get("server") == "CLE_server", "Invalid server response!"
        assert data.get("status") == "running", "Server not running!"
    print("  [OK] CLE_server started and responded on http://127.0.0.1:8765/api/status!")
finally:
    proc.terminate()
    proc.wait()
    print("[TEST] CLE_server terminated successfully.")

print("[TEST] ALL SANDBOX TESTS PASSED!")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
CLEJS - Community GitHub Export Bundler
Prepares a clean, pristine export directory ready to initialize or push to community GitHub.
Sanitizes ephemeral files, personal configurations, scratch test files, and local logs.
"""

import os
import sys
import shutil
import hashlib
from pathlib import Path

ROOT_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
EXPORT_DIR = ROOT_DIR / "dist" / "github_export"

EXCLUDED_DIRS = {
    ".git",
    ".gemini",
    "scratch",
    "test_install_sandbox",
    "dist",
    "__pycache__",
    ".system_generated",
    "python_runtime",  # Downloaded on-demand by DevInstaller
    ".pytest_cache"
}

EXCLUDED_FILES = {
    "server.log",
    "server_test.log",
    "install.log",
    "setup_test.log"
}

EXCLUDED_EXTENSIONS = {
    ".tmp",
    ".log",
    ".pyc",
    ".pyd"
}

def should_exclude(rel_path: Path) -> bool:
    parts = rel_path.parts
    for part in parts:
        if part in EXCLUDED_DIRS:
            return True
    if rel_path.name in EXCLUDED_FILES:
        return True
    if rel_path.suffix.lower() in EXCLUDED_EXTENSIONS:
        return True
    return False

def export():
    print(f"[EXPORT] Preparing clean GitHub export from: {ROOT_DIR}")
    if EXPORT_DIR.exists():
        print(f"[EXPORT] Removing existing export directory: {EXPORT_DIR}")
        shutil.rmtree(EXPORT_DIR)

    EXPORT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    copied_files = 0
    total_bytes = 0

    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(ROOT_DIR):
        # Exclude directories in-place
        dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d not in EXCLUDED_DIRS]

        rel_root = Path(root).relative_to(ROOT_DIR)
        if should_exclude(rel_root):
            continue

        for f in files:
            src_file = Path(root) / f
            rel_file = src_file.relative_to(ROOT_DIR)
            if should_exclude(rel_file):
                continue

            target_file = EXPORT_DIR / rel_file
            target_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            shutil.copy2(src_file, target_file)
            copied_files += 1
            total_bytes += src_file.stat().st_size

    # Ensure clean standard LICENSE and .gitignore
    create_community_metadata()

    print(f"\n[EXPORT] Successfully bundled {copied_files} files ({total_bytes / (1024*1024):.2f} MB)")
    print(f"[EXPORT] Pristine export ready at: {EXPORT_DIR}")

def create_community_metadata():
    gitignore_content = """# CLEJS Community .gitignore
# Dependencies & Runtimes
tools/python_runtime/
tools/PrusaSlicer/
tools/__pycache__/
*.pyc
*.pyo
*.pyd

# Temporary test files & scratch
scratch/
test_install_sandbox/
*.log
*.tmp
*.bak
dist/

# System / Editor caches
.system_generated/
.gemini/
.vscode/
.idea/
Thumbs.db
Desktop.ini
"""
    (EXPORT_DIR / ".gitignore").write_text(gitignore_content, encoding="utf-8")

    license_content = """MIT License

Copyright (c) 2026 JSVCLE Community

Permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to any person obtaining a copy
of this software and associated documentation files (the "Software"), to deal
in the Software without restriction, including without limitation the rights
to use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute, sublicense, and/or sell
copies of the Software, and to permit persons to whom the Software is
furnished to do so, subject to the following conditions:

The above copyright notice and this permission notice shall be included in all
copies or substantial portions of the Software.

THE SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED "AS IS", WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, EXPRESS OR
IMPLIED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO THE WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY,
FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND NONINFRINGEMENT. IN NO EVENT SHALL THE
AUTHORS OR COPYRIGHT HOLDERS BE LIABLE FOR ANY CLAIM, DAMAGES OR OTHER
LIABILITY, WHETHER IN AN ACTION OF CONTRACT, TORT OR OTHERWISE, ARISING FROM,
OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THE SOFTWARE OR THE USE OR OTHER DEALINGS IN THE
SOFTWARE.
"""
    (EXPORT_DIR / "LICENSE").write_text(license_content, encoding="utf-8")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    export()

<#
.SYNOPSIS
    CLEJS Developer Toolchain Installer
    Locates, validates, and installs all required developer tools into the tools directory.
#>

param(
    [switch]$SkipPlaywright = $false,
    [switch]$Quiet = $false
)

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
$ScriptDir = Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Definition
$RootDir = Split-Path -Parent $ScriptDir
$ToolsDir = Join-Path $RootDir "tools"

Write-Host "=================================================" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host "       CLEJS Developer Toolchain Installer       " -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host "=================================================" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host "Root Directory:  $RootDir"
Write-Host "Tools Directory: $ToolsDir"
Write-Host ""

# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Embedded Python 3 Runtime (for runtime & installer bundling)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
Write-Host "[1/5] Checking Embedded Python 3 Runtime in tools\python_runtime..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
$PythonEmbedDir = Join-Path $ToolsDir "python_runtime"
$PythonExe = Join-Path $PythonEmbedDir "python.exe"

if (-not (Test-Path $PythonExe)) {
    Write-Host "  -> Embedded Python not found. Downloading official Python 3.11 embeddable..." -ForegroundColor Cyan
    $Url = "https://www.python.org/ftp/python/3.11.9/python-3.11.9-embed-amd64.zip"
    $ZipPath = Join-Path $ToolsDir "python_embed.zip"
    
    Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $Url -OutFile $ZipPath -UseBasicParsing
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $PythonEmbedDir -Force | Out-Null
    Expand-Archive -Path $ZipPath -DestinationPath $PythonEmbedDir -Force
    Remove-Item $ZipPath -Force
    Write-Host "  [OK] Python 3.11 embeddable runtime installed to tools\python_runtime." -ForegroundColor Green
} else {
    Write-Host "  [OK] Embedded Python 3 runtime is present." -ForegroundColor Green
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Node.js & npm (for bundling & JS AST syntax checks)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
Write-Host "[2/5] Checking Node.js runtime..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
$NodeCmd = Get-Command node -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if ($NodeCmd) {
    $NodeVer = &(node -v)
    Write-Host "  [OK] Node.js is installed ($NodeVer)." -ForegroundColor Green
} else {
    Write-Host "  [!] Node.js not detected in PATH." -ForegroundColor Red
    Write-Host "  -> Attempting install via winget..." -ForegroundColor Cyan
    try {
        winget install OpenJS.NodeJS --accept-package-agreements --accept-source-agreements --silent
        Write-Host "  [OK] Node.js installed via winget." -ForegroundColor Green
    } catch {
        Write-Host "  [WARNING] Please install Node.js manually from https://nodejs.org/" -ForegroundColor Yellow
    }
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Inno Setup 6 Compiler (ISCC.exe for building installer .exe)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
Write-Host "[3/5] Checking Inno Setup Compiler (ISCC.exe)..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
$InnoPaths = @(
    "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\Inno Setup 6\ISCC.exe",
    "${env:ProgramFiles(x86)}\Inno Setup 6\ISCC.exe",
    "$env:ProgramFiles\Inno Setup 6\ISCC.exe"
)

$FoundISCC = $null
foreach ($p in $InnoPaths) {
    if (Test-Path $p) {
        $FoundISCC = $p
        break
    }
}

if ($FoundISCC) {
    Write-Host "  [OK] Inno Setup compiler found at: $FoundISCC" -ForegroundColor Green
} else {
    Write-Host "  [!] Inno Setup compiler not found. Attempting install via winget..." -ForegroundColor Cyan
    try {
        winget install JRSoftware.InnoSetup --accept-package-agreements --accept-source-agreements --silent
        Write-Host "  [OK] Inno Setup installed via winget." -ForegroundColor Green
    } catch {
        Write-Host "  [WARNING] Please install Inno Setup 6 manually from https://jrsoftware.org/isdl.php" -ForegroundColor Yellow
    }
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Python Developer Dependencies (requests, playwright, pyserial)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
Write-Host "[4/5] Checking Python packages & Playwright..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
$DevPython = Get-Command python -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if ($DevPython) {
    Write-Host "  -> Verifying Python development packages..." -ForegroundColor Cyan
    & python -m pip install --quiet requests playwright pyserial
    Write-Host "  [OK] Python packages verified." -ForegroundColor Green

    if (-not $SkipPlaywright) {
        Write-Host "  -> Ensuring Playwright Chromium browser is installed..." -ForegroundColor Cyan
        & python -m playwright install chromium
        Write-Host "  [OK] Playwright Chromium ready." -ForegroundColor Green
    }
} else {
    Write-Host "  [!] Python not found in system PATH." -ForegroundColor Red
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. PrusaSlicer CLI Integration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
Write-Host "[5/5] Checking PrusaSlicer CLI integration..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
$PrusaDir = Join-Path $ToolsDir "PrusaSlicer"
$SystemPrusa = "C:\Program Files\Prusa3D\PrusaSlicer\prusa-slicer-console.exe"

    }
} else {

}

Write-Host ""
Write-Host "==========================================================" -ForegroundColor Green
Write-Host "         CLEJS FULL TREE BUILD & VALIDATION PASSED!       " -ForegroundColor Green
Write-Host "==========================================================" -ForegroundColor Green

@echo off

endlocal
